target_customer: Enterprise revenue leaders (CROs, VPs of Sales, RevOps) at large B2B companies that pay per seat for revenue intelligence
problem: Sales reps do not log most email, calendar and meeting activity in the CRM, so managers lack accurate pipeline data and forecasts.
business_model: B2B enterprise SaaS subscription per seat
product_category: Revenue intelligence and automated sales activity capture (renamed Backstory in 2026)

founders.name: Oleg Rogynskyy
previous_startups: Semantria (text analytics; he was CEO; sold to Lexalytics in 2014)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is Ukrainian-born, moved to the US in the early 2000s and founded People.ai in early 2016. TechCrunch (2014-07-14) names him as Semantria CEO when Lexalytics acquired it; the article does not say he founded it, and a search summary says he started it, so the founder role is not confirmed. Per search summaries of company announcements he handed the CEO role to Jason Ambrose on 2025-10-30 and moved to the board.

founders.name: Kevin Yang
founders.background_notes: YC page says he co-founded People.ai in the Summer 2016 batch and now works on Slack Platform.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed to ingest email, calendar and meeting data across an enterprise and match each activity to the right CRM record with machine learning, plus security and Salesforce integration; hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated activity data and deep CRM integration create stickiness, but the capture idea could be copied by CRM vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (Oct 2018) said People.ai resembled an acquisition target for Microsoft or Salesforce and noted Salesforce was investing more in AI for sales; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Founder thesis in early 2016 was that sales activity data was valuable and not captured properly (SaaStr profile); Lightspeed and Index backed it with a 2017 Series A citing strong Fortune 500 interest.

branding.domain_note: Used the people.ai domain (a country-code .ai domain); no purchase story found. Redirects to backstory.ai after the 2026 rename.

identity.logo: Wordmark; no detailed description in sources opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise AI, with revenue intelligence positioning

rebrands.why: Refocus on giving revenue leaders direct answers rather than data, per company FAQ

branding.community_and_virality: No community, merch or mascot found; coverage is enterprise software and funding press.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name that is hard to search for and was later replaced by Backstory; recognition came from funding news and a unicorn valuation rather than the brand itself.

pivots.why: Strong enterprise and Fortune 500 interest (TechCrunch May 2017)

outcome_analysis: People.ai raised a seed from YC in 2016, a 7 million dollar Series A in 2017, a 30 million dollar Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz in 2018, a 60 million dollar Series C in 2019 and a 100 million dollar Series D in 2021 at a 1.1 billion dollar valuation. It cut staff after the 2020 downturn and renamed itself Backstory in April 2026, and remains active.
notes: Seed of 2.6 million dollars from Y Combinator in Aug 2016 appears only in one aggregator snippet so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Series C 60 million led by ICONIQ: SiliconAngle (2019-05-21, opened) names a16z, Lightspeed, GGV and Y Combinator as participating earlier investors, matching the company press release seen in search results (the people.ai page now redirects to backstory.ai and was not opened). The roughly 500 million dollar valuation is unofficial: SiliconAngle says the company is reportedly worth about 500 million and AIN.UA calls it an unofficial valuation, so it is recorded as reported, not company-stated. Rebrand to Backstory in April 2026 (BusinessWire release, 403 on fetch; seen in search results). CEO change: search summaries say Jason Ambrose became CEO on 2025-10-30 under a planned succession and Rogynskyy moved to the board; no primary page was opened, and the April 2026 rename did not coincide with it. Total raised about 198 to 202 million per aggregators. A headline in search results says People.ai laid off 18 percent of staff and raised a debt round amid COVID-19 uncertainty (about 2020); only the headline was seen. Competitors: TechCrunch May 2017 names Chorus.ai and VoiceOps but as data sources, about nine months after the batch, so not listed. Batch conflict: one a16z-related listing says Spring 2016 while YC says Summer 2016.
